observationInference: Source statements remain research/user requirements. C3/C4 representation, finite support rule and exact-identity prototype boundary are inferences, not observed runtime behavior.

ablations.removedEffect: Without it evidence can be attached but no exact obligation or remainder is identifiable.
Without it arguments collapse the recorded event into a current interpretation; one run cannot preserve distinct outcomes.
Without it every proposed edge could grant support or all domain logic moves into the base.
Without it alternative methods and conjunctive obligations flatten into a bag of attachments.
Without it one observation can silently gain provider scope or stale evidence can regain support.
Without it monotone accumulation of green observations conceals compatible failures.
Loses checkable meaning of support.
Loses AND/OR distinction; allows one strong premise to replace another.
Loses measured outcomes and visible shared blind spots.
Loses compatible reuse or admits invalid cross-scope transfer.
Loses original-failure identity or lets arbitrary newer passes clear a contradiction.
An agent can add a support edge that certifies itself.
Conjunction, alternatives or finite grounding become unsound.
Admits stub-to-provider or cross-configuration transfer.
History and present interpretation collapse.
Code reversion silently reinstates stale authority.
A green alternative or agent dismissal bypasses a recorded counterexample.
A different test can replace the failing obligation.
Duplicates caller tasks or closes broad obligations after narrow findings.
Unknown is silently turned into unconditional optimization veto or permission.
Claims latency from read counts or records infrastructure failure as correctness evidence.

demotions.text: Run is shared provenance metadata of observations, not an additional logical primitive.
Task is a projection of a requested claim and uncovered rule premises, not an authority-bearing primitive.
No universal evidence confidence score survives; retain claim-specific reasons.
Package is a distribution boundary for rules/claims/workflows, not an independently proved runtime module.
Policy is a consumer input, outside proof support; no policy order selected.

modularity: No existing interface/integration test establishes independent implementation modules. Adjacent forms use rule combination, not modular operator claims.
freezeSequence: range untested and nearby negative exclusions
